sources_considered.why: Primary ChatGPT experiments address board comprehension and prompting, but do not isolate the asserted cause in the versions discussed in 2025.
Controlled research identifies an attention-related limitation in other language models; relevant methodological context only.
Causal interventions establish representations in specialized chess models, not in the relevant ChatGPT versions.
Read the primary anecdotal report. It lacks the controls, internal measurements, and complete transcript needed to establish causation.

evidence_items.publisher: Mu-Tien Kuo, Chih-Chung Hsueh and Richard Tzong-Han Tsai / arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The authors report that repeating information can improve board comprehension, while describing continuing problems applying rules. These behavioral interventions do not establish that the 2025 ChatGPT systems never learned a board-and-rules representation.

evidence_items.publisher: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
evidence_items.explanation: This study finds that access to game history matters for chess state tracking in its experimental models. It illustrates why observing poor play alone cannot isolate missing world models as the cause in ChatGPT.

unresolved_gaps: No controlled mechanistic study of the relevant ChatGPT versions was located that isolates absent board-and-rules representations as the cause.
The inspected studies do not distinguish all competing explanations for the reported failures.
ChatGPT's relevant training exposure and internal representations remain unestablished.
